original_text: Upon completion, the document will act as a binding contract between developers and users and will provide a common point of reference for system expectations.

attribute_scores.rationale: The terms used are generally clear, though 'binding contract' carries legal ambiguity in an engineering context.
It fails to specify how agreement is reached, who the signatories are, or when 'completion' is officially recognized.
Consistent with standard document boilerplate, though inconsistent with the core purpose of a technical software requirements specification.
Violates core requirement syntax. It does not use the mandatory modal verb 'shall' and describes document administrative purpose instead of system behavior.
While SRS documents often serve as reference points, defining an engineering document as a legally binding contract is often legally and practically discouraged.
Combines two distinct assertions: acting as a binding contract and providing a common point of reference.
There is no objective, automated, or testable method to verify whether a document successfully acts as a 'binding contract' from a software execution perspective.

layer1.document_understanding_summary: This statement describes the purpose and administrative legal nature of the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document itself within the EVLA WIDAR backend development context, rather than specifying a testable functional capability or behavior of the software system.

layer2.reasoning_summary: All candidate defects are justified. REQ-be_srs-001 is a document meta-statement outlining the purpose of the SRS document itself rather than a verifiable system requirement for the EVLA backend. It lacks normative phrasing, combines multiple assertions, and is untestable by standard software verification methods, failing the applicable standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.

layer3.original_text: Upon completion, the document will act as a binding contract between developers and users and will provide a common point of reference for system expectations.
layer3.refined_text: The EVLA backend system shall provide a common point of reference for system expectations upon documentation completion.
changes_made: Replaced the descriptive, non-normative statement about the document acting as a contract with normative EARS syntax using 'shall' applied to the EVLA backend system.
Removed the non-verifiable contractual assertion ('act as a binding contract') to ensure verifiability and singularity.
Retained the core intent of providing a common point of reference for system expectations.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: The refinement maintains the primary goal of establishing a clear reference point for system expectations while correcting the syntactic and conformance issues by applying proper EARS phrasing and removing untestable legal assertions.

checks.observations: The refinement successfully replaced the non-normative language with 'shall', removed the contractual assertion, and addressed the singularity defect.
The phrase 'upon documentation completion' introduces a temporal ambiguity and shifts the subject from a system functional requirement to a documentation lifecycle process.
No specific protocols or APIs were invented, though the scope was incorrectly shifted to documentation timelines.

The original text was a meta-statement describing the purpose of the SRS document itself. Translating this into a requirement for the 'EVLA backend system' to 'provide a common point of reference' distorts the functional intent, as a backend processing system does not provide documentation reference points.
While it uses the mandatory 'shall' modal, the requirement does not specify a valid EVLA backend system behavior, violating IEEE 29148 system requirements definition criteria.

layer4.critique_and_feedback: The original requirement (REQ-be_srs-001) is fundamentally a meta-requirement describing the purpose of the SRS document, not a technical requirement for the EVLA backend system. While the refiner attempted to fix the syntax by adding 'shall', forcing this non-functional meta-statement into a system requirement results in a nonsensical statement ('The EVLA backend system shall provide a common point of reference...'). Backend correlator systems process signals; they do not serve as documentation reference points. This requirement should be deleted as it belongs to introductory document metadata rather than system requirements.
